newsitem.title: USA: Tanker of Canada crude sold into Calif. - traders.
newsitem.headline: Tanker of Canada crude sold into Calif. - traders.

text.p: Astra Oil Co, a unit of the Argentine energy company Astra CAPSA, sold a 500,000 barrel cargo of Koch Alberta crude into the California market, industry sources said Monday.
Sources declined to name the price of the tanker shipment, but said it would be negotiated off Alaska North Slope (ANS), a bellwether grade on the U.S. West Coast.
Canadian Koch Alberta, with a 33 degree API gravity and one percent sulphur content, is often a substitute for ANS.
Most Canadian crudes are exported through pipelines into the Pacific Northwest, traders said. But they added producers sometimes sell up to two tankers a month into other markets.
Testing on a major Canadian pipeline has left excess light crude in fields and forced producers to scramble to curb weakness in prices.
"They're doing it to remove it from their tradtional market," in the Pacific Northwest, one trader said.
